checks.finding: FEMA's flood map puts this lot in Zone AE (regulatory floodway), a Special Flood Hazard Area (FEMA's 1%-annual-chance floodplain).
checks.limitation: FEMA's zone lines and the parcel lines come from different maps, so the edges may not line up exactly. A flood zone is not a flood-insurance determination or a building permit.

checks.finding: The National Wetlands Inventory maps Riverine (R2UBH) on about 20% of this lot. Franklin County's stream-buffer map puts no part of it in a riparian setback.
checks.limitation: NWI outlines are drawn from aerial imagery (here from 2007) and are approximate: they are not a wetland delineation, and the shares are measured against the mapped OGRIP boundary, not a survey. Filling or building in a wetland or stream can need a Clean Water Act Section 404 permit from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers or a permit from Ohio EPA.

checks.finding: A public road right-of-way (recorded as "Highway") touches this parcel in Franklin County's right-of-way layer, but the county engineer's road layer shows no road centerline running through it beside the parcel. It may be land set aside for a road that was never built, or the edge of a wider road corridor. The nearest mapped road, I-270, is about 43 m (141 ft) away. The road layer lists it in the federal highway system (interstates and expressways), and those are usually limited-access, with no driveways.
checks.limitation: Touching a mapped right-of-way is not legal access. These layers do not show whether the lot has a recorded right to use the road, whether the road is built and maintained where the lot meets it, or whether a driveway would be permitted there.

checks.finding: The seller's right to sell this lot has not been verified.
checks.limitation: This report does not check ownership records or the seller's identity. Sellers who impersonate the real owner often target vacant land (see the linked ALTA guidance).
checks.nextAction: Have a title company confirm the owner of record and reach the owner through contact details it finds independently, not ones the seller supplied.

checks.limitation: The boundary shown comes from Ohio's statewide parcel map (OGRIP), which is not a survey. The real corners and lines can differ.
checks.nextAction: Hire a licensed Ohio surveyor to locate the boundary before you close.
